rationale: The workflow repeatedly fetches and installs pip dependencies (pip upgrade and flake8) on every run with no dependency cache. The repository has pyproject.toml as a cache input, and no equivalent cache step exists. The measured pip-cache experiment (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) added actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/pip keyed on hashFiles('pyproject.toml') before dependency installation and reported ~9.2% elapsed savings while keeping the same install and test steps. This matches P-LIT-GHA-CACHE preconditions (repeated dependency fetching; cache input includes environment/lockfile-like file) and has no contraindication (no mutable/untrusted cached content, no existing cache). Adding the cache step preserves the existing lint coverage and commands, changes no permissions, and adds no secrets, publishing, deployment, or new network access.
